The Police Sub-Inspector of J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the above named accused for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant is running a business by name Sysnet Technologies since 4 years.
On the date of filing of the information, the informant company was dealing with sales and services of the laptops.
The informant has taken the paper publication and also in social media about their services.
On 08.09.2020 the informant was contacted by one Mr.Manoj, wherein he has told that he is the Manager of M/s.Everland Immersive Ltd and he needs laptops on rental basis.
The informant asked him to the submit his requisition through mail.

But,
however the accused has called the informant to come to his Office for discussion.
On 09.09.2020 the informant had been to the office of the accused M/s.Everland Immersive Ltd situated at J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru along with Keerthi Kumar.
The accused had requested around 30 laptops on rental basis and agreed to pay a rent of Rs.4,000/- per month including the GST.
On 10.10.2020 the accused has sent all the relevant documents to the mail of the informant.
The accused has taken 30 laptops on rental basis by depositing Rs.2,00,000/-.
The informant has supplied all the laptops as per the requirement of the accused.
The accused has agreed to execute the Agreement as per the terms and conditions.
But, the accused went on postponing for one or the other reason.
Later, as per the say of the accused, on 11.10.2020 the informant had been to the Office of the accused situated at J.P.Nagar with all the documents.
But, however he was surprised that the door of the said Office was closed.
He enquired his neighbor wherein, he came to know that the accused got flee away by closing his office.
Immediately, the informant had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused persons.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.131/2020 at J.P.Nagar Police Station.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Sub-Inspector of J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against accused No.1 to 5 alleging that they have committed the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to accused No.1 to 5.
On 15.12.2020, accused No.1 to 3 were arrested and produced before the Court on body warrant and remanded to Judicial custody.
On 02.01.2021, accused No.2 was releaed on bail.
On 01.04.2021, accused No.1 was released on bail.
On 24.06.2024, accused No.4 was released on bail.
Later, the case against accused No.1, 4 and 5 was Split Up and the case against Lokesh M vs Moheddin Khureshi Alias Moheen Alias ...

2 accused No.3 was dropped.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to accused No.2 under section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Thereafter, the cognizance was taken for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that accused No.2 has committed offences triable by this court, charges for the offences punishable under Sections 120B,
418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code has been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused persons, the prosecution has examined PW1 to PW5 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

Since, there were no incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidences of the prosecution witnesses against accused No.2, the examination of accused No.2 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.
5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the accused persons.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved the offences charged against accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt?
2. What order or sentence?

7. My answers to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. POINT No.1 :- To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 Lokesh P.N., wherein he has deposed that he has supplied 30 Laptops to the accused company on 08.09.2020.
The accused has deposited an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- and agreed to pay a rent of Rs.4,000/- per month.
The accused had supplied all the relevant documents to the informant.
On the very next month, the informant had been to the office of the accused to take the rent, but he was surprise that the office of the accused was closed.
He has not returned the Laptops.
Immediately the informant had been to the J.P.Nagar Police Station and lodged the information against the accused as per Ex.P1.
Later, the Police have conducted Mahazar as per Ex.P2 and took his signature.
He further has deposed that after 2 months, Byappanahalli Police had caught hold all the accused and seized the Laptops.
Out of 30 Laptops, around 19 Laptops were secured.
9. But in his cross-examination this witness has totally turned hostile and has denied that he has lodged any information against the accused.
Further he finally has deposed that the Laptops were secured and he has compromised the matter with the accused persons.

sentences.text:
The Prosecution has examined CW2/PW2 Naveen Kumar Reddy, CW3/PW3 Michael Angelo,
CW4/PW4 Yogesh M. and CW5/PW5 Venkatesh B.S.
All these witnesses have turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.

They have deposed in their examination-in-chief that they have not supplied any Laptops to accused No.1 to 5 on rental basis and they have not lodged any information to the Police Station against this accused.
Since the Laptops were secured, all these witnesses have compromised the matter with the accused persons and turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.

11. In order to prove the charges leveled against the accused persons, out of 38 witnesses cited in the Police Report by the Investigation Officer, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of five witness before this Court as PW1 to PW5.
On perusal of the above evidences, it appears that the First Informant CW1/PW1 has turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
CW2 to CW5 are examined as PW2 to PW5.
They have deposed in their cross-examination that their statement was not recorded by the police and they do not have any knowledge of the case.
They have compromised the matter.
Since PW1 to PW5 have turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution, this Court finds that the purpose will not be served in examining the rest of the witnesses.
For this reason, the evidences of the other Prosecution witnesses from CW6 to CW38 are dropped.

Under these circumstances, I am holding that the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

12. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, accused No.2 is not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against him.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDERS  Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C,
accused No.2 is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 418, 419, 420,
465, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bond and surety bond executed under Section 437 of Cr.P.C. will be in force till appeal period and thereafter they shall be canceled.

Office is hereby directed to keep the entire file with Split up and 5.

Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
